entry_moment: A person sends a first message, taps the call button, or submits a form. The moment is theirs, not yours
exit_criterion: You have sent a reply that a human wrote or approved
may_be_counted: Count of contacts by source. This is the only honest top-of-funnel number a chat business has
may_not_be_counted: A lead. Nobody has qualified anything yet, and the word lead applied here is what makes every rate below it look bad
vn_channel_note: Zalo, Messenger, TikTok and marketplace chat all deliver here. Marketplace chat is the one you cannot export, so it needs a manual tally or it silently drops out of the count
what_it_does_not_prove: That the person wants to buy. A price question and a wrong-number message enter this state identically

exit_criterion: A qualification question has been answered, either way
may_be_counted: Response time per contact, and the share answered inside your declared target
may_not_be_counted: A conversation. Sending a greeting template is not a conversation, and counting it as one is how a response-rate metric gets gamed against its own purpose
vn_channel_note: Facebook, Zalo and the marketplaces each publish a response metric on their own dashboard. Read yours in the account rather than trusting a number quoted from a blog post
what_it_does_not_prove: That the reply was read or understood

entry_moment: Fit and intent are both answered yes, by evidence in the thread rather than by hope
exit_criterion: A price has been given in writing
may_be_counted: Qualified count, and the share of new contacts reaching it
may_not_be_counted: A commitment. Qualified means worth your hours, nothing more
vn_channel_note: In chat the qualifying answer usually arrives unprompted in the first two messages: the district, the quantity, the date of the event. Read before you interrogate
what_it_does_not_prove: That they can pay. Fit is your judgement of match; it is not a credit check

entry_moment: You have written down which criterion failed
may_be_counted: Disqualified count by reason, which is the table that tells you whether your targeting is wrong or your criteria are
may_not_be_counted: Nothing about the person. A disqualification is a statement about fit with this offer, on this day
vn_channel_note: Wrong-district, wrong-budget and wholesale-enquiry are the three that dominate a Vietnamese retail inbox. If one of them is most of your volume, the ad targeting is the problem, not the inbox
what_it_does_not_prove: That they will never buy. Disqualified is not blacklisted

entry_moment: A specific price for a specific scope is stated in writing in the thread
exit_criterion: They respond to the price, in either direction
may_be_counted: Quote count and quoted value. The first pipeline number with money in it that is not a guess
may_not_be_counted: Revenue. A quote is your number, not theirs
vn_channel_note: Quoting inside chat is the norm here, so the quote has no document behind it unless you make one. Screenshot or paste the scope with the price or the scope will be argued later
what_it_does_not_prove: That the price was accepted or even read

entry_moment: They ask for a change to price or scope
exit_criterion: Agreement or refusal, stated by them
may_be_counted: Concession given per deal, which is the number that shows discounting as a habit rather than a decision
may_not_be_counted: Progress. A long negotiation is as often a slow no as a near yes
vn_channel_note: Haggling is expected, not an objection. What is not expected is a discount with nothing asked in return - volume, timing, a review, a referral, cash instead of COD
what_it_does_not_prove: That the deal is nearly closed

entry_moment: They have committed: paid, placed the order, or confirmed in writing
may_be_counted: Won count and won value. Divide by contacts for the only conversion rate that matters
may_not_be_counted: A delivered order. On cash-on-delivery the gap between won and delivered is real money
vn_channel_note: COD means a won order can still fail at the door. check_tracking_plan.py already carries this correction with --purchases and --delivered; use it before reporting revenue

entry_moment: They said no, bought elsewhere, or the deadline passed
may_be_counted: Loss count by reason - but read what_it_does_not_prove before acting on the reason column
may_not_be_counted: The reason. A reason you inferred is a guess with a label on it
vn_channel_note: Price is the reason people give and the reason sellers record, because it ends the conversation politely. It is over-reported in every self-recorded loss log, and this is a house-rule caution rather than a cited finding
what_it_does_not_prove: That price was the cause. If price is recorded the field asks what the gap was and what else was true

entry_moment: No response from them after your follow-up ladder is exhausted
may_be_counted: Stalled count by the state they stalled in, which localises where your process loses people
may_not_be_counted: A loss you can explain. Stalled is the absence of information
vn_channel_note: Silence in chat is not refusal and not a reason to keep sending. Whether you may contact again at all is a legal question - lifecycle-retention.md and lifecycle-duties.csv decide it
what_it_does_not_prove: That they lost interest. The message may never have been delivered or seen
